newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa's Ramaphosa tipped as next Eskom chairman.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa's Ramaphosa tipped as next Eskom chairman.

text.p: New Africa Investments Ltd deputy chairman Cyril Ramaphosa has been tipped to become the next chairman of electricity utility Eskom, according to reports in the South African press on Friday.
Public Enterprises Minister Stella Sigcau had approached Ramaphosa and shorltlisted him to replace current chairman John Maree when he stepped down, the reports said.
The Ministry could neither confirm nor deny the speculation, while Ramaphosa told Business Day newspaper: "I don't know what you are talking about."

But Allan Morgan, Eskom's chief executive officer told the Weekly Mail & Guardian that it would be "good speculation" to say Ramaphosa would succeed Maree when the government decided to appoint a new chairman.
Ramaphosa was unavailable for comment on Friday.

He recently spearheaded the acquisition of Anglo American Corp's 48 percent stake in Johnnies Industrial Corp Ltd by the National Empowerment Consortium -- a black economic empowerment grouping of labour and business.
Ramaphosa is also the president of the Consitutional Assembly which is currently involved in revising the draft of the South African constitution rejected by the Constitutional Court on September 6.
Eskom is one of the various South African parastatals which is being considered for partial privatisation, a process which black business sees an opportunity for enhancing economic empowerment.
